name: STAVE
expansion: Small-sample Tests of ABCD Variants and Estimators

intro.problem: The barrel region is data-starved: it holds too few background events to train on comfortably and too few to give the ABCD closure test real power, so a barrel closure test can pass simply because its error bars are too wide to fail.
intro.value: Techniques that recover usable statistics from a small region would let data-driven background estimation work where it cannot yet be trusted, and would separate estimators that close on merit from ones that only appear to.
intro.approach: STAVE is a set of barrel studies run against one shared baseline: a closure term built around the statistical noise floor, decorrelation and closure-weight sweeps across four loss configurations, and a network pretrained on the higher-statistics endcap and fine-tuned on the barrel. The joint-background model is developed in KERF and applied here.
intro.goals: The outcome is a reproducible barrel baseline, each technique scored on closure with honest uncertainties against that baseline, and a clear statement of which techniques actually recover statistical power in the barrel and which do not.

questions: Does a barrel closure test carry real evidence, or do wide error bars simply absorb a same-size error?
Does a closure term built around the barrel's statistical noise floor improve closure, alone or combined with decorrelation?
Can a network pretrained on the higher-statistics endcap transfer to the barrel without importing the endcap's biases?

timeline.label: First barrel test of the noise-floor closure term on a small sample
Literature review of how barrel and endcap are handled in ABCD and LLP searches
Barrel ideas deck: baseline re-run first, then closure term, pretraining and joint-background model
Baseline re-run graded with a pre-registered evaluation framework
Reframed as the barrel program; joint-background model moved to KERF
Run the four loss configurations across the λ and μ grid
Replicate the noise-floor closure term across seeds
Test endcap pretraining against a barrel-only control
Apply the KERF joint-background model to the barrel

tagline: Barrel program: techniques for a data-starved region

components.name: DNC_FLR
components.subtitle: Noise-floor closure term
components.summary: A closure-aware loss term that subtracts the expected statistical noise floor from the measured closure error, with no hinge, so training is penalized only for non-closure the data can actually resolve. Built for low-count regions; early barrel evidence is promising but thin and needs a replicated grid.

components.name: Loss sweeps
components.subtitle: λ and μ across four configurations
components.summary: Every configuration is swept on the same shared grid and graded with the same pre-registered closure framework, so the arms are directly comparable. λ weights the decorrelation penalty; μ weights the closure term.

items.label: BCE
items.detail: Plain classifier, no penalty: the control every other arm is measured against

items.label: BCE + DNC_FLR
items.detail: Noise-floor closure term, swept in μ

items.label: BCE + DNC_FLR + DisCo
items.detail: Both terms, swept on the λ × μ grid

components.name: Endcap pretraining
components.subtitle: Borrow statistics from the larger region
components.summary: Train on the endcap, which has a far larger background sample, then adapt to the barrel. Only the features both regions share can transfer, and a barrel-only network trained from scratch is the control.

items.label: Fine-tune
items.detail: Pretrain the whole network on the endcap, then fine-tune on the barrel

items.label: Shared trunk
items.detail: One trunk trained on both regions, with a separate head per region

items.label: Frozen trunk
items.detail: Freeze the endcap trunk and train only a barrel head

links.title: Shared baseline
links.text: Every STAVE technique is scored against the barrel baseline locked in BASELINE, with the same data-health gate and the same closure measurement, so an improvement is a measured difference rather than a change of yardstick.

links.title: Joint probability model
links.text: Instead of removing the dependence between the two discriminants in training, model the joint background directly and use it for the barrel's ABCD estimate. The model is built and vetted in KERF; STAVE is where it is applied to the barrel.
